section_summary: This section documents the establishment, regulation, and revision of charges for port facilities and terminal services furnished to foreign vessels in Japanese ports under SCAP occupation. It includes August 1947 rate schedules and Circular No. 16, State Department correspondence regarding Far Eastern Commission policy, and SCAPIN 1927 directing the Japanese Government to resume responsibility for commercial port and terminal operations effective October 1, 1948. The section concludes with SCAP initiating a comprehensive review of the Japanese port rate structure against historical and contemporary rates worldwide.

subfiles.about: SCAP directive transferring commercial port and terminal operations to the Japanese Government, with attached regulations and rate tariffs.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP directive transferring responsibility for civilian relief and commercial port, terminal, and customs operations at Tokyo-Yokohama and Kobe to the Japanese Government effective October 1, 1948. Inclosure 1 sets forth governing conditions and reimbursement procedures in dollars or yen, while Annexes A and B provide comprehensive tariff schedules for stevedoring, port entry, equipment hire, longshoring, lighters, tugs, and trucking.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1927: Japanese Port Operations and Charges for Port Facilities and Terminal Services

subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Telegram announcing a comprehensive review of Japanese port rates and requesting 1941 and current rate data for Far Eastern, Middle Eastern, Western, and European ports.
subfiles.title: Telegram ZX 30098: Review of Rates for Port Facilities in Japan
subfiles.to: Department of the Army, Department of State, and Others
